skill_title: Solve circuit problems with internal resistance
notes: 20 items: 13 lifted, 7 fresh. EMF = I(R + r); terminal voltage; reading EMF from an open switch; effect on terminal voltage when R is added or removed.

items.question: Define EMF of a battery in TWO ways: (a) in terms of energy, and (b) as measured directly in a circuit.
items.expectedAnswer: (a) The energy supplied per unit charge by the battery; (b) the terminal voltage measured when no current flows (open circuit).
items.explanation: (a) ε = W/Q (energy per charge); (b) ε = V_terminal at I = 0.
options: (a) The energy used per unit charge by the resistor; (b) the voltage across the largest resistor.
(a) The energy supplied per unit charge by the battery; (b) the terminal voltage measured when no current flows (open circuit).
(a) The current per unit charge; (b) the voltage measured at full load.

items.question: Which of the following CORRECTLY defines the EMF of a cell?
options: The potential difference across the terminals when current flows
The maximum energy (work done) per unit charge by the cell
The product of current and external resistance
The internal resistance times the current
items.expectedAnswer: The maximum energy (work done) per unit charge by the cell
items.explanation: EMF = max work per coulomb = total energy supplied per charge by the cell.

items.question: In a circuit, the terminal voltage of a battery equals its EMF when:
options: Maximum current flows
No current flows
Internal resistance is large
External resistance is zero
items.explanation: V_terminal = ε − Ir. When I = 0 (open switch), V_terminal = ε.

items.question: A voltmeter across a battery reads 2.8 V when the external switch is OPEN and 2.63 V when the switch is closed (current 0.85 A flows). Calculate the internal resistance of the battery.
items.explanation: Open: ε = 2.8 V. Closed: V_terminal = 2.63 V. V_lost = ε − V_terminal = 0.17 V. V_lost = Ir ⇒ r = 0.17/0.85 = 0.2 Ω.

items.question: Continuing: the voltmeter reads 2.8 V with the switch OPEN. What is the EMF of the battery?
items.explanation: Open switch ⇒ I = 0 ⇒ V_terminal = ε. So ε = 2.8 V (the open-circuit voltmeter reading).

items.question: A 4 Ω resistor draws 0.8 A from a battery with internal resistance r = 0.5 Ω, giving terminal voltage 3.2 V across the resistor. Calculate the EMF of the battery.
Explain why a battery HEATS UP during operation.
items.expectedAnswer: Current through the battery's internal resistance dissipates power (P = I²r) as heat.
items.explanation: Internal resistance ⇒ power lost as heat. The bigger I or r, the more heating.
options: The chemical reactions release light, which warms the battery.
The external resistors push heat back into the battery.
Current through the battery's internal resistance dissipates power (P = I²r) as heat.

items.question: A battery (ε = 12 V, r = 0.5 Ω) drives a circuit with external resistance 6 Ω. Calculate the current from the battery.
Continuing: with I = 1.85 A and r = 0.5 Ω, calculate the terminal voltage of the battery.
A battery (ε = 9 V, r = 1 Ω) drives a circuit with external resistance 5.4 Ω. Calculate the current.
Continuing: voltmeter across the battery terminals reads what value when I = 1.41 A flows?
In a circuit with R₁ (series) and R₂ ∥ R₃ (parallel), R₃ is suddenly DISCONNECTED. Explain qualitatively what happens to the brightness of R₁.
items.expectedAnswer: Dimmer — removing the parallel branch raises the total resistance, lowering the current through R₁.
items.explanation: Removing a parallel branch increases R_parallel and thus R_total. Less current ⇒ less power dissipated in the series resistor ⇒ dimmer.
options: Dimmer — removing the parallel branch raises the total resistance, lowering the current through R₁.
Brighter — removing R₃ lets more current flow through R₁.
Unchanged — R₁ is in series, so its current is fixed.

items.question: If R₁ in the external circuit is INCREASED, what happens to the terminal voltage of the battery? Explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Terminal voltage increases — higher R lowers the current, so the lost volts (Ir) across the internal resistance fall.
items.explanation: Less current ⇒ less voltage dropped internally ⇒ more voltage available externally.
options: Terminal voltage decreases — higher external resistance always lowers the terminal voltage.
Terminal voltage increases — higher R lowers the current, so the lost volts (Ir) across the internal resistance fall.
Terminal voltage stays equal to the EMF regardless of R₁.

items.question: A battery has external resistors and switches S1 and S2. When S1 is OPEN and S2 is CLOSED, only certain branches conduct, and ammeter A2 reads 3.64 A. The simplified external resistance in this state is 1.42 Ω and the battery has internal resistance r = 0.5 Ω. Calculate the EMF of the battery.

In a circuit with parallel branches controlled by switches, S₂ (controlling one parallel branch) is OPENED. Describe the effect on the (a) ammeter reading in the main line, (b) brightness of a bulb in the remaining parallel branch.
items.expectedAnswer: The main ammeter reading decreases — opening a parallel branch raises the total resistance, lowering the total current.
items.explanation: Removing a parallel branch: R_total ↑, I_total ↓, V_terminal ↑, current in remaining branch ↑, brightness ↑.
options: The main ammeter reading increases — fewer branches means more current overall.
The main ammeter reading is unchanged — the main-line current is fixed by the battery.
The main ammeter reading decreases — opening a parallel branch raises the total resistance, lowering the total current.

items.question: A battery with EMF 9 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω drives a current of 2 A through an external circuit. Calculate the external resistance.
A battery has EMF 6 V and internal resistance 1 Ω. It is connected to a 2 Ω resistor. Calculate the voltmeter reading across the 2 Ω resistor.
items.explanation: I = 6/(2 + 1) = 2 A. V_R = IR = 2 × 2 = 4 V. (This equals the terminal voltage.)

items.question: A battery is short-circuited (connected directly across its terminals with negligible external resistance). If EMF = 4 V and r = 0.2 Ω, calculate the short-circuit current.
items.explanation: Short circuit: R_ext ≈ 0. I_max = ε/r = 4/0.2 = 20 A. This is the largest current the battery can deliver — usually dangerous (burns out the battery).

items.question: A 12 V battery with r = 0.2 Ω is connected to a circuit. When the main switches are open, only one branch (e.g. with R_Z) carries current and the ammeter reads 1.3 A. Calculate the voltmeter reading across the battery terminals.
A learner says: 'The internal resistance of a battery is fixed at zero in idealised problems.' Is the second part of that statement correct, and what's the point of including a non-zero r?
items.expectedAnswer: Only ideal cells have r = 0; real cells have r > 0, which lowers the terminal voltage when current flows.
items.explanation: Ideal: r = 0. Real: r > 0 causes voltage drop and heating during current flow.
options: Only ideal cells have r = 0; real cells have r > 0, which lowers the terminal voltage when current flows.
Correct — all batteries have zero internal resistance.
Correct — internal resistance only matters in AC circuits.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_EMF_DEF_ENERGY: EMF energy definition missing 'per unit charge'
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_EMF_DEF_OPEN_CIRCUIT: EMF circuit definition missing 'no current / open switch'
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_EMF_VS_TERMINAL_VOLTAGE: Confuses EMF with terminal voltage when current flows
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INTERNAL_R_FROM_LOST_VOLTAGE: Wrong arithmetic in r = V_lost / I
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_EMF_EQN_SETUP: Wrong form of ε = I(R + r) or V_terminal = ε − Ir
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INTERNAL_RESISTANCE_HEATING: Can't explain why internal resistance causes heating
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INTERNAL_R_FORGOT_IN_TOTAL: Forgets to include r in total resistance
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PARALLEL_RULES: Misstates how adding/removing parallel branches affects R
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_IDEAL_VS_REAL_BATTERY: Doesn't distinguish ideal cell (r=0) from real cell
